title: Python Interview Practice — Exceptions & File Handling
topics: Understand exceptions, errors, and common built-in exception types.
Catch and handle expected runtime failures safely.
Understand exactly when else and finally execute.
Raise exceptions deliberately for validation and control flow.
Open files using appropriate modes and manage file resources.
Use read, readline, readlines and iteration to process files.
Write, append and generate file content safely.
Use with open to manage resources automatically.
Combine exceptions, loops, functions, collections and file handling.

topicQuestions.question: Which mode opens a file for reading only?

topicQuestions.question: Which mode opens a file for appending without erasing existing content?
hints: This mode adds new content to the end of the file.

topicQuestions.question: Which method writes a string to an open file object?

topicQuestions.question: Which mode allows both reading and writing without erasing existing content?

topicQuestions.question: Why is 'with open(...) as f' preferred over manual open()/close() calls?

topicQuestions.question: Which special methods must a class implement to support the with statement?

topicQuestions.question: Which block runs no matter whether an exception occurred, commonly used for cleanup?

topicQuestions.question: Why is catching the broad Exception class often discouraged?

hints: A broad except clause catches almost everything, expected or not.

topicQuestions.question: What is the correct order when catching both a specific and a general exception?

If a general exception (like Exception) comes first, it would catch everything, making a later specific clause unreachable.
